function: Learned downlink pilots, user-side CSI compressors with quantization and entropy coding, and a BS network computing precoders directly from feedback bits, trained end-to-end (pp. 5-6).
system: Downlink FDD massive MIMO: BS with Nt=64 antennas (ULA), single-antenna users, 1-10 cells with 1-6 users per cell, no RIS; carrier frequency not stated (pp. 3, 9).
method: Fully connected networks for pilots, user compressors and BS precoder with entropy coder; end-to-end training on a rate-minus-overhead loss (unsupervised, no labels); pretraining and BS fine-tuning (pp. 5-9).
data_channel: Custom ULA multipath simulator, 2 paths, CN(0,1) gains, uniform AoD; at least 10^9 random training realizations, separate test set of at least 10^4 per user (p. 9).
test_conditions: Same channel statistics in train and test; SNR mismatch (train 0/10/20 dB or a range) with BS fine-tuning; users pretrained at K=1 reused for larger K (pp. 9-12).
baselines: Non-learned: MRT and ZF with perfect CSIT. Learned: [18]-like reconstruction-oriented compressor plus MRT/ZF, binary-feedback precoding design of [21]; own bounds with CSIT or uncompressed feedback (p. 10).
metrics: Achievable network sum rate (bits per channel use) versus feedback overhead in bits per user (entropy estimate); split of overhead between desired and interfering CSI (pp. 7, 10-11).
q1_support: p. 8: "we consider the following multipath channel model for our" simulations, similar to [21]; p. 9 gives 2 paths, i.i.d. CN(0,1) gains and uniform AoD. No 3GPP, DeepMIMO, or measured channel is used, so the channel is a custom simulator.
q2_support: p. 11: "with fixed pretrained users, the BS is fine-tuned" (users pretrained for K = 1, Fig. 6 on p. 10 goes to K = 6); p. 12: "used at a different SNR. Moreover, we also consider the same" models after BS-only fine-tuning.
q3_support: p. 9: "reconstruction-oriented systems that rely on traditional precoding schemes such as maximal-ratio transmission (MRT)" and ZF, with perfect-CSIT references; p. 10: "results in [21, Fig. 4 and 9], where the feedback is modeled" as binary values (earlier learned method), and "reconstruction-oriented system (similar to [18]) followed by" ZF; all on sum rate versus overhead (Fig. 5).
q4_support: p. 9: "consists of four fully-connected" layers is the only size information (layer widths). No parameter count, FLOPs, runtime, or complexity order is reported; p. 11 only says in words that the BS network grows with K.
q5_support: p. 9: "entropy bottleneck class from [31], which provides a PyTorch" implementation is a third-party library. Channels come from the paper's own model (Eqs. 30-31), and no link to its own code or data is given.
notes: Included. Area 2 chosen because the stated problem is the CSI feedback overhead-performance tradeoff (title and abstract, p. 1; linear precoding is 'the downstream task', p. 2). The BS network also outputs the precoders and the metric is the sum rate, so area 3 is the alternative reading if the reviewer weighs the metric. q1 is 0: custom 2-path ULA simulator (pp. 8-9). q2 rests on users pretrained at K=1 and reused for larger K with BS-only fine-tuning (pp. 9, 11) and on the train/test SNR mismatch with BS fine-tuning (p. 12), not on an SNR sweep alone. q3: non-learned references are MRT and ZF with perfect CSIT (Fig. 5, p. 10); the conventional 'reconstruction-oriented followed by MRT/ZF' scheme uses a learned compressor similar to [18]; the earlier learned method [21] is taken from its published results (p. 10). Reviewer may check whether perfect-CSIT ZF/MRT is accepted as the non-learned baseline.
